sections.h2: Which written notice a Michigan landlord must give
sections.html:
The notice depends on the landlord's reason. Unpaid rent brings a 7-day notice. A month-to-month tenancy ends on one month's notice, and a year-to-year tenancy ends one year after service. Most of these rules sit in MCL 554.134, with the court filing rules in MCL 600.5714.

Michigan's court administrators publish fill-in forms for each notice. The Demand for Possession for nonpayment is form DC 100a, the general Notice to Quit is DC 100c, and the drug activity notice is DC 100e. Each form comes in a tenant copy and a court copy. The landlord keeps the court copy along with the record of how and when the notice was delivered.

Michigan eviction notice types and how many days each gives
Reason for noticeNotice periodStatute
Nonpayment of rent7 days554.134(2); 600.5714(1)(a)
Periodic or at-will tenancy1 month, or the rent interval when rent is paid more often than every 3 months554.134(1)
Year-to-year tenancyEnds 1 year after service554.134(3)
Controlled substance on the premises, with a formal police report24 hours554.134(4); 600.5714(1)(b)
Caused or threatened physical injury to someone, police notified7 days600.5714(1)(e)
Serious health hazard or extensive damage7 days after demand to leave or repair600.5714(1)(d)

The court's checklist for both the 7-day demand and the notice to quit has four steps. A landlord who can't answer yes to each may have trouble later in court:

  • Fill in the form completely, including the tenant's name, the delivery address, the rent owed or the move-out date, and the landlord's own address and phone.
  • Sign it.
  • Deliver the tenant's copy by one of the permitted methods.
  • Keep the court copy, whose certificate of service records the date of delivery, the name of the person who received it and how it was delivered.

That certificate is the landlord's evidence when the case reaches the judge. Fill it in on the day of delivery rather than rebuilding it afterward.

The court forms list four valid ways to serve it:

  • Hand it to the tenant in person.
  • Give it on the premises to a family or household member or the tenant's employee, with a request to pass it on.
  • Mail it first class to the last address you have for the tenant. For mail, MCL 600.5718 sets the service date as the next regular delivery day after mailing.
  • Email it, but only if the tenant consented to electronic service in writing and confirmed that consent by reply.

The forms warn about improper service. Slipping the notice under the door, leaving it outside the door, attaching it to the property or mailing it by a method that requires a signature can all sink the later court case. The 7-day nonpayment form is the minimum, and the lease or another law may require a longer period.

sections.h2: What happens after the notice period ends
sections.html:
The landlord can file a complaint in district court. The state court forms for the complaint ask for a copy of the notice or demand. The court then issues a summons.

  • Trial is set within 10 days of the summons being issued, and service must happen 3 or more days ahead of it. Courts with a local rule may instead require appearance 5 days after service.
  • A summary proceeding is heard within 7 days after the tenant appears or the trial date arrives, with adjournments only by stipulation.
  • A case based on the 24-hour drug activity notice is heard on the day the tenant appears and is adjourned only for extraordinary reasons.

If the court finds for the landlord on nonpayment, it fixes the amount due at trial and subtracts any rent excused by the landlord's breach of the lease or statutory covenants. The tenant can stop the writ by paying that amount plus taxed costs within the time provided (MCL 600.5741 and 600.5744(7)).

sections.h2: When a sheriff or court officer can remove a tenant
sections.html:
Only after the court orders it. MCL 600.5744 directs the court to issue a writ of restitution commanding a court officer, bailiff or sheriff to put the landlord in possession and remove occupants and property. Ordinarily the writ waits 10 days after judgment.

The court may allow an immediate writ on conditions it sets. Examples: the premises were ordered vacated for lack of a housing certificate, entry was forcible, the occupant is a trespasser, the tenant is causing a serious health hazard or extensive damage, or the case involves drug activity. A land contract forfeiture carries a longer wait: 90 days if under half of the price was paid, six months if half or more.

sections.h2: Lock changes and utility shutoffs are unlawful
sections.html:
MCL 600.2918 treats force, changing locks without handing over keys, boarding up the premises, removing doors or windows, keeping or destroying the tenant's belongings, and cutting off heat, water, electric or gas as unlawful interference. The tenant may claim the larger of real damages or $200 for each incident.

Someone pushed out by force may recover triple actual damages or $200 if that is more, along with possession. A suit to regain possession is due within 90 days of the event or its discovery, and a damages suit within a year. A lease can't waive the section. Exceptions cover court orders, brief entry for repairs or inspection, and a good-faith belief that the tenant has abandoned the home and left rent unpaid.

sections.h2: Selling a house with a tenant in it
sections.html:
A rented house can often be sold occupied, but a sale doesn't let the seller bypass the notice rules. The tenancy still ends only through the notice and court steps above. A buyer who wants vacant possession has to wait out the lease or have the seller serve a proper notice first.

A few sale situations have their own rules. After a mortgage foreclosure sale or an execution sale, a person who stays past the redemption period can be removed by summary proceedings under MCL 600.5714(1)(g). After a sale by a personal representative under probate court license, the same remedy applies under paragraph (h). Following a foreclosure sale, the purchaser may inspect and, if inspection is unreasonably refused or damage is imminent, may start summary proceedings after giving the mortgagor 7 days' written notice to repair (MCL 600.3238).

Phone the clerk of the district court that covers the rental for local rules and the filing fee.

sections.h2: Planning a sale around the notice clock
sections.html:
Work backward from the date you want the buyer to take possession. Add the notice period for your tenant's situation, then the court steps: the summons and trial, any wait for a writ, and the removal itself. A cash buyer can close quickly, so the tenant timeline often becomes the slowest part of the sale.

  • Pull the lease, the rent record and any notice already served.
  • Pick the notice that matches your reason, not the one that sounds fastest.
  • Tell the buyer in writing whether the house will close occupied or empty.

If you'd rather not run the eviction yourself, a buyer who takes the house occupied is one way to sell without waiting on the court calendar.

faqs.q: How many days is a Michigan eviction notice for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Seven days. A landlord may end the tenancy with a written 7-day notice to quit under MCL 554.134(2), and MCL 600.5714(1)(a) opens summary proceedings if the tenant stays past 7 days after a written demand. A lease may call for longer.

faqs.q: Can a Michigan landlord evict someone with a 24-hour notice?
faqs.a: Only for controlled substance activity when the lease has a termination clause and a formal police report has been filed. Under MCL 554.134(4) the notice is 24 hours. Other violations use longer notice periods.

faqs.q: Does a Michigan landlord need a court order to remove a tenant?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the notice runs out, the landlord files in district court, obtains a judgment and then waits for a writ of restitution, ordinarily 10 days later. Court officers or the sheriff carry it out.

faqs.q: What if a Michigan landlord changes the locks without a court order?
faqs.a: The tenant may recover actual damages or $200, whichever is greater, per occurrence under MCL 600.2918, and may recover possession. A tenant should file within 90 days to regain possession.

faqs.q: How much notice does a monthly tenant get?
faqs.a: One month. If rent is payable at intervals shorter than 3 months, the notice period equals the payment interval. A year-to-year tenancy ends 1 year after service of the notice.
